Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

die verb

also pass away, dead, be dead, death, die of

classical

Cic. Sen. 74: moriendum enim certē est
Traupman 77

morior, morī, mortuus sum

verb, third conjugation (-iō), deponent; future participle moritūrus

What one dies of goes in the ablative: famē morī, to die of hunger (Cic. Att. 6.1.6, Lewis & Short). Plants die too: a bush sī exāruit, moritur, if it dries out, dies (Varr. LL 5.102). Moriar, sī …, may I die if … (Cic. Att. 8.6.4).

Other words

  • mortuus, mortua, mortuum — dead

    also used · classical · Catull. 3.3: passer mortuus est; Phaedr. 3.16.19: sīc vīva quod negārat tribuit mortua

  • dēcēdō, dēcēdere, dēcessī, dēcessum — pass away

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.6.2: pater nōbīs dēcessit

    The gentle word of letters; in full dē vītā dēcēdere (Lewis & Short).

  • animam efflāre — breathe one’s last

    phrase: anima with efflō · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.19 (Lewis & Short, s.v. anima)

  • mors, mortis f. — death

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 6.21.1: omnium rērum mors est extrēmum (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • passer mortuus est meae puellae, passer, dēliciae meae puellae

    my girl’s sparrow is dead, the sparrow, my girl’s petCatull. 3.3–4

  • pater nōbīs dēcessit

    our father has passed awayCic. Att. 1.6.2

  • Moriendum enim certē est, et incertum an hōc ipsō diē.

    For die we certainly must, and no one knows whether it will be this very day.Cic. Sen. 74

See also be born, live, life, kill.
